expectations.text: Presents the top tier first as the anchor and makes the middle tier the visibly best value
expectations.evidence: The anchor half is met: Gold is in the first column, labelled '(anchor)', and the text says 'Present Gold first as the anchor.' The best-value half rests only on labels. Silver is marked '(best value)' and called 'the default the card points at', but the numbers don't back this up. Gold costs EUR 6,000 for 6 passes and Silver costs EUR 3,000 for 3 passes, so both work out to EUR 1,000 per pass. Gold also adds first pick of table position, the largest logo class, and an intro call. On that basis Gold is equal or better value. expectations.text: Presents the top tier first as the anchor and makes the middle tier the visibly best value
expectations.evidence: The Packages table lists Headline Partner (8,000) first, so the top tier comes first and works as an implicit anchor. The card never says it is an anchor. Gold (5,000) is not shown as the best value: it has no 'best value' or 'most popular' label, no callout, and no per-pass or per-benefit comparison. Gold is cheaper per pass (1,250) than Headline (1,333) or Silver (1,500), but the reader has to work that out. Gold does get prime position and its own guide page, but nothing frames it as the sweet spot. The first half of the item is met. The second half is barely touched.
